State vs Ashish Jain on 30 September, 2024 
 In The Court Of Ms. Richa Sharma, Additional Chief
 Judicial Magistrate-01, Tis Hazari Court, Central Delhi
 State Vs. Ashish Jain
 Fir No. 95/2021
 Ps Pahar Ganj
 U/s 279/338 Ipc
 Date of Institution of case: 25.06.2021
 Date of Judgment reserved:-28.09.2024
 Date on which Judgment pronounced:30.09.2024
 Judgment
 Cr. Case No. : 7387/2021  Date of : 12.04.2021  Commission  of offence  Name of the : SMT. MANJU SAGAR  complainant  Name of the : ASHISH JAIN S/o Sh. Rajeev Jain R/o  accused H. No. 7643/29-C, Tel Mil Marg, Gali  person No. 1, Ram Nagar, Nabi Karim, Delhi. 
 Offence : U/s 279/338 IPC  complained of  Plea of : Not guilty  accused  Date of order : 30.09.2024  Final Order : ACQUITTED FIR No. 95/2021 State Vs. Ashish Jain PS Paharganj Page No. 1 of 24  THE STORY OF PROSECUTION IS AS UNDER:
1. The case of the prosecution is, that on 12.04.2021, at around 05:45 am, at Chames Ford Road,
within the jurisdiction of PS Paharganj, accused was found driving vehicle bearing registration No.
DL-8CAE-4068 on a public place in a manner so rash and negligent as to endanger human life or the personal safety of others. Further, while driving so, accused hit the complainant, namely, Manju Sagar, while driving the above vehicle in the aforesaid rash and negligent manner, due to which complainant sustained grievous injuries. According to prosecution, accused committed offences punishable under Section 279/338 of The Indian Penal Code, 1860.

1 INVESTIGATION 2. After registration of the case, necessary investigation was carried out by the IO concerned. Site plan was prepared. Statements of witnesses were recorded under Section 161 of the Criminal Procedure Code, 1973 (hereinafter to be referred as Cr.PC. for brevity). Relevant record was collected. The final report under Section 173 of Cr.P.C., was prepared against the above named accused and challan was presented in the Court. 
3. Copies of challan and relevant documents were supplied to the accused free of costs as envisaged under Section 207 of Cr.P.C.
CHARGE 4. A prima facie case under Sections 279/338 IPC, was found to be made out against the accused. 
Notice was framed upon the accused accordingly. The accused pleaded not guilty and claimed the trial. Thereafter prosecution examined its witnesses and a brief synopsis of their testimony is as under:-
FIR No. 95/2021 State Vs. Ashish Jain PS Paharganj Page No. 2 of 24 PW1 COMPLAINANT SMT. MANJU SAGAR 5. PW1 deposed, that on 12.04.2021, she was going for evening walk to Roop Singh (Railway)
Stadium from her house. At about 05:45 PM, she had crossed the road and she was on right side of her path. In the meantime, one vehicle bearing registration no. DL-8CAE-4068, came from wrong side. PW1 stated, that as per her memory the registration no. of the offending vehicle was DL-8CAE-4068. 
The said offending vehicle hit her on her right hip and as an impact, she jumped up in the air and she was thinking as if she would survive or not. Thereafter, she fell down on the ground and the weight of her body was on her left hip. The driver who was driving the offending vehicle at a high speed stopped the offending vehicle after the accident. Public persons gathered at the spot and they tried to lift her up. Public persons lifted her from there and kept her on the footh-path. PW1 further deposed, that she was not in a position to call anyone. One auto wala took her mobile phone and called her husband. 
Thereafter, her husband called her neighbour and her neighbour called at 100 number. Thereafter,
PCR van came at the spot. Staffs of PCR van took her to Railway Central Hospital and admitted her in the said hospital. Her maid namely, Lovely informed her neighbor regarding the accident. Her neighbours also came at the hospital. Thereafter, police recorded her statement, Ex. PW1/A.
Witness correctly identified the photographs of the offending vehicle, Ex. P1 (colly). 
Upon asking the leading question by the Ld. APP for the State, witness stated, that on 12.04.2021, he was going for evening walk to Karnail Singh Stadium.

2 This witness was cross-examined by the Ld. Counsel for accused. Court observation: The registration no. of the offending vehicle was found written on the left hand palm of the witness in black ink. 
FIR No. 95/2021 State Vs. Ashish Jain PS Paharganj Page No. 3 of 24 PW2 SMT. LOVELY 6. PW2 deposed, that she does not remember the date and month, however, it was in year 2021,
when the incident took place. In the evening, while she was going for cooking food, at that time she was watching her mobile and she heard a noise. She saw that one lady was lying in injured condition, on the road. One vehicle bearing No. DL-8CAE-4068 was also standing there. She clicked photograph of the said vehicle. She narrated the above incident to the police. Thereafter, police shifted the injured to Railway Hospital. Witness correctly identified the photographs of the offending vehicle, Ex. P1 (colly). 
This witness was examined by the Ld. APP for the State as she was resiling from her previous statement. 
This witness was cross-examined by the Ld. Counsel for accused. 
PW3 SH. ANUJ KUMAR 7. PW3 deposed, that in the year 2022, in afternoon, he was coming from Railway Station, Pahar Ganj side by his car and he saw that an accident had already occurred on the road going from CP towards Paharganj. Some public persons told, that one lady who was crossing the road was hit by some vehicle. Thereafter, he made call on 100 number and police reached the spot. The injured lady was shifted to hospital. Police obtained his particulars, recorded his statement and thereafter, he left the spot. PW3 further deposed, that he had not seen the driver of the offending vehicle. 
This witness was examined by the Ld. APP for the State as this witness was not disclosing the complete facts on the point of identity of the accused as well as the offending vehicle. 
This witness was not cross-examined by the Ld. Counsel for accused despite opportunity being given to do so. 
FIR No. 95/2021 State Vs. Ashish Jain PS Paharganj Page No. 4 of 24 PW4 HC RAJEEV KATARIYA ARREST WITNESS 8. PW4 deposed, that on 12.04.2021, he was on emergency duty from 08:00 AM to 08:00 PM and at about 06:00 PM, an information was received regarding the present case vide DD No. 63A with respect to an accident. Thereafter, he alongwith IO/ASI Chander Pal went to the spot and they came to know that an accident took place and injured had already been taken to Northern Railway Central Hospital, Delhi, by PCR Van.

3 He remained at the spot and IO/ASI Chander Pal went to the hospital and after some time, IO returned to the spot and handed over to him the rukka of the present case for registration of the FIR. Accordingly, he went to the PS and got the FIR registered through Duty Officer. After registration of the FIR, he returned to the spot and handed over the copy of FIR and original rukka to the IO. IO recorded his statement U/s 161 Cr.PC. 
This witness was cross-examined by the Ld. Counsel for accused. 
PW5 DR. ASTHA KAPOOR, PG-1, UCMS, GTB HOSPITAL 9. PW5 deposed, that on 12.04.2021, the patient, namely, Smt. Manju Sagar was brought to the hospital for medical examination as injured had suffered injuries in road accident. She examined the patient vide MLC No. 58/21 and after medical examination she gave her first aid and referred the patient to Surgery and Ortho department for further evaluation and management. The detailed description of the injury suffered had been mentioned in the said MLC, Ex. PW5/A. This witness was cross-examined by the Ld. Counsel for accused. 
PW6 SH. GURDEEP SINGH, EX. ASI/TECH. (MECHANICAL EXPERT)
10. PW6 deposed, that on 17.04.2021, he was called by the IO for mechanical examination of the vehicle at the PS. Accordingly, he visited PS and at the instance of IO, he conducted mechanical inspection of vehicle i.e. car FIR No. 95/2021 State Vs. Ashish Jain PS Paharganj Page No. 5 of 24 bearing registration no. DL8CAE4068 make Hyundia I10. After mechanical inspection of the said vehicle, he submitted his report to the IO, Ex. PW6/A. This witness was cross-examined by the Ld.
Counsel for accused. 
PW7 SI CHANDER PAL INVESTIGATING OFFICER 11. PW7 deposed, that on 12.04.2021 he was on emergency duty from 8.00 am to 8.00 pm. The information about the present case was received vide DD no. 63A qua the accident. Thereafter, he along with Ct. Rajeev went to the spot at CF road, Paharganj, Delhi. At the spot, he came to know that injured had been taken to hospital by PCR van. Thereafter, he asked Ct. Rajeev to remain at the spot and he went to the Northern Railway Central Hospital. 
In the hospital, the injured namely Mrs. Manju Sagar was found admitted. He collected her MLC from the hospital. He inquired the injured about the accident and recorded her statement in the hospital. He made endorsement on complaint and prepared rukka i.e Ex. A2. Thereafter, he returned to the spot and handed over said rukka to Ct. Rajeev for registration of FIR. 
Accordingly, he went to PS and got FIR registered. After registration of FIR, Ct. Rajeev returned to the spot and handed over the copy of FIR and original rukka to him. Thereafter, he prepared site plan of the spot at the instance of servant of complainant namely Ms. Arti exhibited as Ex. PW- 7/A.
Thereafter, he served notice u/s 133 MV Act i.e Mark A to Smt. Shalini Jain, who was the wife of accused Ashish Jain. On 14.04.2021 he went to the hospital and at that time accused Ashish Jain State vs Ashish Jain on 30 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/199419680/
4 was found present in the hospital along with injured Manju Sagar. He interrogated accused Ashish Jain and thereafter, he was arrested vide arrest memo i.e Ex. PW-7/B. Personal search of accused was also conducted vide personal search memo i.e Ex. PW-7/C. The offending vehicle was produced by the accused and the same was seized vide seizure memo i.e Ex. PW-7/D. Accused produced his DL and FIR No. 95/2021 State Vs. Ashish Jain PS Paharganj Page No. 6 of 24 same was also seized vide seizure memo i.e Ex. PW-7/E. Accused also produced original RC, photocopy of insurance certificate and PUC of the vehicle and same was seized vide memo i.e Ex. PW-7/F. Thereafter, he recorded disclosure statement of accused i.e Ex. PW-7/G. Thereafter, accused was released on furnishing of bail bond as the offence was bailable. He recorded the statement of witnesses u/s 161 CrPC. 
During investigation, mechanical inspection of the offending vehicle was got conducted through mechanical expert namely Gurdeep Singh on 17.04.2021 and he obtained his report. He obtained medical documents of the injured from the hospital and also obtained opinion on MLC which was grievous in nature. Thereafter, he prepared charge sheet against accused for the offence u/s 279/338 IPC and filed the same before the court. 
Witness duly identified the offending vehicles in photographs. This witness was duly cross examined by the Ld. Defence counsel. 
12. Pursuant to examining of all the prosecution witnesses, prosecution evidence was closed on 30.08.2024 and the matter was listed for recording of statement of accused U/s 313 Cr.PC.
STATEMENT UNDER SECTION 313 CR.PC 13. After completion of prosecution evidence, statement of accused under Section 313 Cr.P.C. was recorded. All incriminating material brought on record were put to the accused, to which he denied the allegations made against him and claimed himself to be innocent and pleaded that he has been falsely implicated in this case. Accused did not lead evidence in his defence. Thereafter, the matter was listed for final arguments. 
14. On the basis of the above oral and documentary evidence on record, Learned APP requested for conviction of the accused and severe punishment as FIR No. 95/2021 State Vs. Ashish Jain PS Paharganj Page No. 7 of 24 per law. 
15. On the other hand, learned defence counsel contended that the prosecution has miserably failed to establish the guilt of the accused beyond all reasonable shadow of doubt as prosecution has as such failed to establish the rashness and negligence on the part of the accused in the present case. 
Accordingly, he prayed for the acquittal of the accused. 
16. I have heard the arguments advanced at length by the prosecution as well as the Ld. Counsel for the accused and have further perused carefully the evidence on record. My findings in detail are as under:

5 POINT FOR DETERMINATION: 
17. This Court has weighed the rival submission made on behalf of the State as well as on behalf of defence in light of the testimonies and material appearing on record. It is observed, that in the present case the accused has been charge-sheeted for the commission of offence punishable under Sections 279 and 338 of IPC, to which the accused pleaded not guilty and claimed trial. In order to prove commission of offence, the following point arise for determination:
(i) Whether Manju Sagar sustained injuries in road accident that occurred on 12.04.2021 as a result of rash and negligent driving of accused Ashish Jain via vehicle bearing registration no. DL-8CAE-4068. 
ANSWER TO POINT FOR DETERMINATION:
I) No. FIR No. 95/2021 State Vs. Ashish Jain PS Paharganj Page No. 8 of 24 REASONS FOR DETERMINATION 18. The onus lies on the prosecution to prove these allegations against the accused. 
19. In the present case, charges brought against the accused are under Sections 279 and 338 of IPC for driving the vehicle in question in a rash and negligent manner and thereby causing injury to the complainant namely, Manju Sagar. The prosecution in order to bring home the guilt of the accused examined seven witnesses in its evidence. In order to prove the guilt of the accused, it was incumbent upon the prosecution to prove:
Firstly, that accident in question took place;
Secondly, accused was driving the vehicle in question at that relevant point of time and Thirdly, accused was rash and negligent in driving the vehicle in question as a result of which the complainant / injured sustained injuries as embodied in MLC Ex.
PW-5/A. The star witness examined by the prosecution in the present case is PW1 i.e.
Smt. Manju Sagar as she is the injured who sustained injuries in the alleged accident. 
It is material to anatomize the testimony of PW1 in order to bring home the guilt of the accused. It is deposed by PW1, that on 12.04.2021 she was going for an evening walk and at about 5.45 pm she had crossed the road and was on the right side of her path, when the offending vehicle came from the wrong side and hit against her. It is material to note, that PW1 in her examination in chief did not remember the registration number of the offending vehicle and she had stated, that said registration number only after the reading the same from the inscription that was written on the left hand palm of her's. The said observation was categorically made by Ld.
Predecessor as under:
State vs Ashish Jain on 30 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/199419680/
6 "Court observation : The registration number of the offending vehicle was found written on the left hand palm of the witness in blank ink." 
FIR No. 95/2021 State Vs. Ashish Jain PS Paharganj Page No. 9 of 24 Thus, from the above observation of the Ld. Predecessor of this court it can be deduced, that the witness did not remember the registration number of the offending vehicle while making her deposition before the court. 
PW1 further deposed in her examination in chief, that vehicle had hit her on her right hip and as a result of the impact she fell on the ground. She further deposed, that the driver of the offending vehicle came at a high speed and pursuant to the accident public persons gathered at the spot and thereby lifted her up. It is material to note,
that as per the narrative of PW1 one auto wala took her mobile phone and made a call to her husband and thereafter, her husband called the neighbour and resultantly, the neighbour made a call at 100 number. Thus, as per the narrative of PW1, the prosecution ought to have examined the auto wala, the husband of the complainant,
the neighbour who eventually made the 100 number call. Further, as per PW1, its her maid who informed her neighbour and resultantly her neighbour also came to the hospital where she was taken by the staff of PCR van. 
This witness was subjected to cross examination by the Ld. APP for the State, as she did not depose anything regarding the date on which the alleged accident took place. 
It is further material to note, that the witness was also subjected to litmus test of cross examination by the Ld. Defence Counsel whereby she deposed, that her statement was recorded only once that is on the date of the alleged accident itself. It is further not out of place to mention, that witness categorically deposed, that due to Covid-19 the police officials had not met her but they got certain papers signed from her while remaining outside. Meaning thereby, that it was incumbent upon the prosecution to prove that the said papers that were got signed from the complainant /
injured were signed after making her understand the emote of it. Further, no light is thrown by the prosecution on the nature of the documents / papers that were got signed from the injured by the police officials. 
FIR No. 95/2021 State Vs. Ashish Jain PS Paharganj Page No. 10 of 24 It is apposite to note, that during the cross examination of the injured, various improvements have been recorded in comparison to the statements that were narrated by her during investigation. PW1 deposed in her cross examination, that she had stated to the police in her complaint, that she had crossed the road and was on the right side of the footpath. She further stated, that she had told in her complaint, that vehicle bearing no. DL8CAE4068 was coming from the wrong side. Not only this, she further stated,
that she had told in her complaint, that the offending vehicle hit her on her right hip and as an impact of the same she was jumped up in the air and was thinking if she would survive or not. She further deposed, that she had told in her complaint, that one auto driver took her phone and informed her husband but it is pellucid to note,
State vs Ashish Jain on 30 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/199419680/
7 that on being confronted with her complaint Ex. PW1/A no such statements were found to be recorded. Therefore, it can be safely deduced, that there were material improvements in the testimony of PW1 while she made her deposition before the court. 
It is further material to note, that during her examination in chief, PW1 deposed, that one auto wala took her phone and called her husband and thereafter, her husband called her neighbour and in turn it is her neighbour who made a call at 100 number but in her cross examination she deposed, that she does not know if after making call to her husband, the auto wala made any call to 100 number or not. 
It is apposite to note, that as per the narrative of PW1, her neighbour Amit Mahajan reached at the spot and accompanied her to the hospital but the said Amit Mahajan has not been examined by the prosecution as one of the witnesses. It is pellucid to note, that it was imperative upon the prosecution to have examined Amit Malhotra as it is he who had made the call at 100 number as per the story of the prosecution and it is he who had arrived at the spot of the alleged accident pursuant to the receipt of the phone call from the husband of the complainant and it is he who had accompanied the FIR No. 95/2021 State Vs. Ashish Jain PS Paharganj Page No. 11 of 24 complainant to the hospital and therefore, his examination was vital as various material aspects as per the story of the prosecution had surfaced in his presence and non-examining of this witness per se puts a dent in the story of the prosecution. 
Admittedly, as per the case of PW1, police had not recorded the statement of Amit Mahajan in her presence. 
It is averred by PW1, that there was no zebra crossing at the spot of the accident and therefore, admittedly, the complainant had not crossed the road by using the zebra crossing. It is further relevant to note, that the complainant had not shown the actual place of accident to the IO and therefore, a question marks arises with regard to actual identification of the spot vide the site plan showing the depiction of the accident in question. Admittedly, as per the narrative of PW1 she had only informed about the place of incident to the IO. The relevant excerpts of her cross examination to this effect are as under:
"I cannot tell if there was zebra crossing at the spot. There was no divider at the spot. 
I had shown the place of accident to the IO. Again said, I had not sh own the place of accident to the IO. (Vol. I had informed about the place of accident to the IO.)" 
Thus, per se from the testimony of PW1 the culpability of the accused beyond reasonable doubts cannot be attracted as there are material contradictions in the testimony of PW1 as compared to the her narrative made by her in her statement recorded during investigation. Therefore, it is vital to examine the testimony of other prosecution witnesses to appreciate the story of the prosecution. 
State vs Ashish Jain on 30 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/199419680/
8 Prosecution examined Lovely as PW2. Admittedly, she neither remembered the date nor did she remember the month in which the alleged accident took place and despite being cross examined by Ld. APP with regard to the date of alleged incident being 12.04.2021, PW2 deposed, that she cannot tell whether the date of incident was 12.04.2021 or not. Now as per the testimony of PW2, she heard some noise and thereafter saw, that one lady was FIR No. 95/2021 State Vs. Ashish Jain PS Paharganj Page No. 12 of 24 lying in an injured condition on the road, meaning thereby, that PW2 got to know about the alleged accident from the noise that she heard. She further deposed, that she saw that one lady was lying on the road in an injured condition and that one vehicle bearing no. DL8CAE4068 was also standing there. Thus, from the testimony of PW2 it can be deduced, that she only heard the noise regarding the alleged accident but did not see the accident happening and what she saw at the spot was only that a lady was lying and that a vehicle was standing. As per the testimony of PW2 admittedly, she was not the eye witness to the alleged accident as she had not seen the accident happening or transpiring. It is material to note, that the witness did not depose anything with regard to the mode and the manner in which the alleged vehicle was being driven and it was only on being cross examined by the Ld. APP for the state, that the witness admitted that the driver of the offending vehicle was driving the vehicle at a high speed.
This witness was subjected to litmus test of cross examination by the Ld. Counsel for the accused and admittedly, nothing could surface from the entire deposition of PW2 to establish that PW2 had actually witnessed the accident in question. Thus, the testimony of this witness does not lend any credence to the story of the prosecution. 
Thereafter, prosecution examined PW3 Anuj Kumar. He deposed, that in the year 2002 somewhere in the afternoon, he was coming from Paharganj side in his car when he saw that accident had already occurred on the road and some public persons told that one lady who was crossing the road was hit by some vehicle. Thereafter,
PW3 made a call at 100 number and police reached the spot. 
At this stage, court deems it fit to halt and deliberate into the testimony of PW3, as it can nowhere be deciphered from the testimony of PW3 as deposed by him in his examination in chief, that he was the driver of the auto who had taken the phone of the injured and made a call to her husband. Further, FIR No. 95/2021 State Vs.
Ashish Jain PS Paharganj Page No. 13 of 24 as per the testimony of PW3, he was coming in his car from the side of railway station and thus, the factum that he was driving the auto on the fateful day also does not stand substantiated from his testimony per se. Another material aspect is that PW3 deposed, that it was somewhere around afternoon when he saw that an accident already occurred on the road but as per the narrative of PW1 she had crossed the road somewhere around 5.45 pm. Thus, there is a major discrepancy with regard to the time depicted by PW3 of the accident from the one depicted by PW3. Further, PW3 told in his testimony,
that he made a call at 100 number and there is no iota of whisper with regard to any State vs Ashish Jain on 30 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/199419680/
9 call being made by PW3 to the husband of the complainant. Thus, the entire chain of event as depicted by PW1 in his examination in chief, whereby she stated, that one auto wala took her phone and called her husband and thereafter, her husband called her neighbour and resultantly her neighbour called at 100 number remains unproved and further contradicted as it is averred by PW3, that 100 number call was made by him. No evidence has been led by the prosecution to clear air regarding this discrepancy and the above elucidated contradictions. 
PW3 further was cross examined by Ld. APP for the State as he was not disclosing the complete facts. On being cross examined, the witness totally denied the contents of the statement of his that were recorded u/s 161 CrPC as Ex. PW-3/A and further stated, that he had never stated any of this to the police. He not only denied seeing the accident but further denied seeing the accused i.e the driver of the offending vehicle. He further averred, that he was only informed about the accident by the public persons. PW3 further failed to identify the photographs of vehicle i.e Ex. P1 colly that were shown to him. 
Admittedly it is the narrative of PW3, that he was informed by public persons who had gathered at the spot that a lady had met with an accident but the prosecution did not examine any of the eye witness despite they being present at the spot.
FIR No. 95/2021 State Vs. Ashish Jain PS Paharganj Page No. 14 of 24 20. At this stage, court deems it fit to place reliance on the case laws pertaining to non examination of public witnesses. 
21. In case titled as Roop Chand Vs. State of Haryana reported as CC Cases 3 (HC), it was held as that where the police has failed to join independent witnesses in the investigation despite their availability and further failed to take action against those who refused to take part in investigation nor their names were noted down by the police, the explanation of the police for not joining independent witnesses is an afterthought and liable to be rejected. 
22. In the case of Sahib Singh v. State of Punjab AIR 1997 SC 2417, it has been held as under:-
"Having gone through the record we find much substance in each of the above contentions. Before conducting a search the concerned police officer is required to call upon some independent and respectable people of the locality to witness the search. In a given case it may so happen that no such person is available or, even if available, is not willing to be a party to such search. It may also be that after joining the search, such persons later on turn hostile. In any of these eventualities the evidence of the police officers who conducted the search cannot be disbelieved solely on the ground that no independent and respectable witness was examined to prove the search but if it is found-as in the present case-that no attempt was even made by the concerned police officer to join with him some persons of the locality who were admittedly available to witness the recovery, it would affect the weight of evidence of State vs Ashish Jain on 30 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/199419680/
10 the Police Officer, though not its admissibility." 
23. In the case of D.V. Shanmugham v. State of A.P., AIR 1997, SC 2583, it has been observed as under:-
"It also appeared from the evidence of PW-2 and PW-8 that there were several other people who witnessed the occurrence and they are not the residents of that locality. If such independent witnesses were available and yet were not examined by the FIR No.
95/2021 State Vs. Ashish Jain PS Paharganj Page No. 15 of 24 prosecution and only those persons who are related to the deceased were examined then in such a situation the prosecution case has to be scrutinized with more care and caution."
24. In the case of Pawan Kumar Vs. The Delhi Administration, 1989 Cr.LJ 127 Delhi, in which it was observed as follows:
"Kalam Singh has to admit that at the time of the arrest and recovery of the knife,
there was a lot of rush of public at the bus stop near Subhash Bazar. According to Jagbir Singh, he did not join any public witness in the case while according to Kalam Singh, no public person was present there. It hardly stands to reason that at a place like a bus stop near Subhash Bazar, there would be no person present at a crucial time like 7.30 pm when there is a lot of rush of commuters for boarding the buses to their respective destinations. Admittedly, there is no impediment in believing the version of the police officials but for that the prosecution has to lay a good foundation. At least one of them should have deposed that they tried to contact the public witnesses or that they refused to join the investigation. Here is a case where no effort was made to join any public witness even though number of them were present. 
No plausible from the side of the prosecution is forthcoming for not joining the Independent witnesses in case of a serious nature like the present one. It may be that there is an apathy on the part of the general public to associate themselves with the police raids or the recoveries but that apart, at least the IO should have made an earnest effort to join the independent witnesses. No attempt in this direction appears to have been made and this, by itself, is a circumstance throwing doubt on the arrest or the recovery of the knife from the person of the accused.''
25. In the case of Sadhu Singh Vs. State of Haryana 2000 (2) CC Cases HC 73, the Court took note of the fact that public witnesses were not joined in investigation to acquit the accused. 
FIR No. 95/2021 State Vs. Ashish Jain PS Paharganj Page No. 16 of 24 26. In the case of Massa Singh Vs. State of Punjab 2000 (2) C.C. Cases HC 11,
conviction was set aside on the ground that it was obligatory on the part of investigating officer to take assistance of independent witnesses to lend authenticity to the investigation conducted by him. It was observed as under:-
State vs Ashish Jain on 30 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/199419680/
11 "The recovery has been effected from a public place. The Investigating Officer could have taken the trouble to associate an independent witness to get the attestation of such independent witness regarding the authenticity of the investigation conducted by him. This aspect of the case has not been properly appreciated by the Court below." 
27. In the case of Chanan Singh Vs. State,1986 Crl. Rev. No.720 (P&H) 94, it was held that it was obligatory on the part of the police to join independent witnesses and the statement of official witness that witnesses refused to join investigation was rejected as an afterthought. 
28. In the cases of Gurbel Singh Vs. State of Punjab, 1991 Crl.Rev. No.504 (P&H) and Dhanpat Vs.
State of Punjab, 2000 (1) CC Cases HC 52, it has been held that non-joining of independent witnesses is fatal to the prosecution case and accused is entitled to benefit of doubt. 
29. At this stage, I also deem it fit to state, that apart from above reasons, in order to bring home the guilt of the accused U/s 279/338 IPC, the prosecution ought to have established the necessary ingredients for attracting culpability under the above mentioned sections. It was incumbent upon the prosecution to have proved the existence of the elements of criminal negligence and rashness on behalf of the accused in present case. In order to prove commission of offence, the following point arise for determination:
(i) Whether Manju Sagar sustained injuries in road accident that occurred on 12.04.2021 as a result of rash and negligent driving of accused Ashish Jain via vehicle bearing registration no. DL-8CAE-4068.
summary.ANALYSIS:
19. In the present case, charges brought against the accused are under Sections 279 and 338 of IPC for driving the vehicle in question in a rash and negligent manner and thereby causing injury to the complainant namely, Manju Sagar.
The prosecution in order to bring home the guilt of the accused examined seven witnesses in its evidence.
In order to prove the guilt of the accused, it was incumbent upon the prosecution to prove:
Firstly, that accident in question took place;
Secondly, accused was driving the vehicle in question at that relevant point of time and Thirdly, accused was rash and negligent in driving the vehicle in question as a result of which the complainant / injured sustained injuries as embodied in MLC Ex.
PW-5/A.
Meaning thereby, that it was incumbent upon the prosecution to prove that the said papers that were got signed from the complainant /
injured were signed after making her understand the emote of it.
Further, no light is thrown by the prosecution on the nature of the documents / papers that were got signed from the injured by the police officials.
It is pellucid to note, that it was imperative upon the prosecution to have examined Amit Malhotra as it is he who had made the call at 100 number as per the story of the prosecution and it is he who had arrived at the spot of the alleged accident pursuant to the receipt of the phone call from the husband of the complainant and it is he who had accompanied the FIR No. 95/2021 State Vs. Ashish Jain PS Paharganj Page No. 11 of 24 complainant to the hospital and therefore, his examination was vital as various material aspects as per the story of the prosecution had surfaced in his presence and non-examining of this witness per se puts a dent in the story of the prosecution.

Thus, per se from the testimony of PW1 the culpability of the accused beyond reasonable doubts cannot be attracted as there are material contradictions in the testimony of PW1 as compared to the her narrative made by her in her statement recorded during investigation.

At this stage, court deems it fit to halt and deliberate into the testimony of PW3, as it can nowhere be deciphered from the testimony of PW3 as deposed by him in his examination in chief, that he was the driver of the auto who had taken the phone of the injured and made a call to her husband.
Further, FIR No. 95/2021 State Vs.
Ashish Jain PS Paharganj Page No. 13 of 24 as per the testimony of PW3, he was coming in his car from the side of railway station and thus, the factum that he was driving the auto on the fateful day also does not stand substantiated from his testimony per se.
In the case of Sadhu Singh Vs. State of Haryana 2000 (2) CC Cases HC 73, the Court took note of the fact that public witnesses were not joined in investigation to acquit the accused.

FIR No. 95/2021 State Vs. Ashish Jain PS Paharganj Page No. 16 of 24 26.
In the case of Massa Singh Vs. State of Punjab 2000 (2) C.C. Cases HC 11,
conviction was set aside on the ground that it was obligatory on the part of investigating officer to take assistance of independent witnesses to lend authenticity to the investigation conducted by him.
28. In the cases of Gurbel Singh Vs. State of Punjab, 1991 Crl.Rev. No.504 (P&H) and Dhanpat Vs.
State of Punjab, 2000 (1) CC Cases HC 52, it has been held that non-joining of independent witnesses is fatal to the prosecution case and accused is entitled to benefit of doubt.
It was incumbent upon the prosecution to have proved the existence of the elements of criminal negligence and rashness on behalf of the accused in present case.

Therefore, placing reliance on the above law, Court deems it fit to deduce that non-examination of public witnesses / eye witnesses has proved fatal to the case of prosecution.
30. Further, in deciding the question as to whether the accused was guilty of rash or negligent act within the scope of above sections, the court has to judge as to the amount of care and circumspection which a prudent and reasonable man is said to be having regard to all the circumstances of the case.
Therefore, to come to the conclusion regarding the fragment of care and circumspection, it was further incumbent upon the prosecution to have established other peripheral factors like the existence of any red light at the place of the incident, was there any speed breaker,
the existence of any by lane or the reasons for the accused be driving on the wrong side of the road and whether there was existence of any zebra crossing at the point where victim has allegedly stated to be hit by the offending vehicle.
I get strength from the judgment of Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in Mahadeo Hari Lokre Vs. P. Maheshvara AIR 1792 SC 221.

FIR No. 95/2021 State Vs. Ashish Jain PS Paharganj Page No. 18 of 24
Similarly in the case in hand,
no matter how much circumspect or vigilant the accused was a driver, if the injured had suddenly crossed the road, the accused could not have saved the accident.

Another major discrepancy that can be observed with regard to mechanical inspection report is as per the report Ex. PW-6/A certain damages were identified in the offending vehicle, however as per the deposition of PW6 made before the court, he categorically stated, that the offending vehicle had only scratch marks and there was no damage.
At this stage, I also deem it fit to state, that apart from above reasons, in order to bring home the guilt of the accused U/s 279/338 IPC, the prosecution ought to have established the necessary ingredients for attracting culpability under the above mentioned sections.
It was incumbent upon the prosecution to have proved the existence of the elements of criminal negligence and rashness on behalf of the accused in present case.
Merely, because the statement of the witnesses is to the effect, that the driver i.e. alleged accused was driving the offending vehicle on the alleged date of the incident, does not suffice to prove the guilt of the accused.
The prosecution has to prove the manner in which the vehicle was driven and how such driving was rash or negligent.
It cannot be said with precision that the accused had to take some extra care while passing through spot.
Perusal of the site plan, would show, that the accused was driving the vehicle on proper/correct side of the road and even no zebra crossing was marked on the site plan.
It is settled proposition of law, that burden is on the prosecution to prove as how the accused was rash or negligent in driving the offending vehicle.
It cannot be presumed, that the accused must have been driving the vehicle in rash or negligent manner only because one person had met with an FIR No. 95/2021 State Vs. Ashish Jain PS Paharganj Page No. 21 of 24 accident on the road while crossing it from a place where there was no zebra crossing or any perfect signal.
33. Even otherwise, if for the sake of arguments it is perceived, that the accused was driving the offending vehicle on the fateful day and the version of the prosecution is believed to be a gospel truth, it further was incumbent upon the prosecution to prove rashness and negligence on the part of the accused as guilt can not be imposed upon a person simply because he was driving the alleged State vs Ashish Jain on 30 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/199419680/
14 offending vehicle on the fateful day or at the time of the accident as the necessary ingredients to bring home the guilt u/s 279/338 IPC is to prove the rashness and negligence
and in this case no iota of evidence has been led by the prosecution on these aspects.

Therefore, in the teeth of above analysis this court finds no hesitation in deducing ,that Firstly, the testimony of the tectonic witnesses i.e complainant suffer from inter se material contradictions and therefore, she is not a reliable witness of the prosecution.

Secondly, the prosecution has though projected two eye witness i.e the driver of the auto and maid of the complainant but both of them had outrightly denied to the seeing of the accident.
Further, as per the prosecution witnesses public persons had gathered at the spot but they have not been examined by the prosecution for the reasons best known to it.
Therefore, the rashness and negligence on the part of the accused does not stands established.
34. Additionally, court cannot be unmindful of the fact, that no doubt wrong acquittals are undesirable and shake the confidence of the people in judicial system, much worse, however, is the wrongful conviction of the innocent man.
The consequences of conviction of innocent men are far more serious and its reverberation would be felt by an innocent all his life in a civilized society,

therefore, it is the duty of the court to avoid any wrongful conviction and to grant benefit of doubt where ever the need arises.
If two views are possible, one favouring the accused and the other against him, the benefit of doubt must be given to the accused and in the instant case, prosecution has failed to prove its case against accused beyond reasonable doubt.
35. At this stage, court further deems it fit to state, that it is a settled principle of criminal jurisprudence that culpability cannot be established on surmises and conjectures but it should rest on cogent, reliable and clinching evidence, dispelling every doubt and bulwarking the fact that in all possibility, the offence must have been committed by the accused.
